done_when: Close checks each --dismiss against the item's open findings before it runs tests or review, and accepts a dismissal of an open finding from an earlier round

known.title: Dismissal evidence can be tied to the wrong commit
Retaining an omitted finding can invalidate the required review check
Check dismissal numbers after reconciling the item's remote review

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - The default branch inserts a proof line into an existing file, and close reuses an earlier review after merging it.
The check at src/forge/close.py:682-683 verifies only that the cited line number exists in the reviewed commit, not that it is the line cited in the current checkout. If the new proof is inserted at line 20 and the older file already had a line 20, close accepts that unrelated old line and keeps the older commit as the dismissal baseline. A later edit to the inserted proof appears only as an addition in the diff from that baseline, so the check at src/forge/review.py:654-675 does not reopen the finding even though its evidence changed.
findings.title: Dismissal evidence can be tied to the wrong commit

why: A close with --dismiss runs the full tests and review, then refuses the dismissal because it checks only the new repair review's findings, so the whole run is wasted (#1253)
